claims.text: Data center revenue is still growing year over year.
queries: Data Center revenue increase compared to prior year
claims.rationale: The claim is about past and current results, and the filings support it directly. Data Center revenue was up year over year in the latest quarter (117%) and in the prior quarter (92%), and tagged annual figures show growth as well. The risk-factor passages are context about future volatility, not evidence against the claim.

claims.text: A small number of customers account for a large share of revenue.
queries: loss of a key customer risk
claims.rationale: [Commentary withheld: it cited a number (23%) that is in none of the claim's verified quotes or cited figures.]

claims.text: Export controls on sales to China are restricting revenue.
claims.rationale: The filings show export controls on China caused a charge and sharply limited licensed China sales. Reported China revenue is mixed: down for the fiscal year, up strongly in the latest quarter. The passages do not measure how much revenue the controls cost.

The passages show a recovery, not a steady expansion. Gross margin rose year over year in the first half of fiscal 2027, but part of that is the absence of the prior-year $4.5 billion H20 charge, and the company says it was approximately flat sequentially. The last full fiscal year saw a decline. The claim holds if it means a rebound from the depressed fiscal 2026 level and is not supported if it means margins are still rising.

claims.text: The company depends on a limited number of suppliers to manufacture its products.
claims.rationale: The risk factors state directly that the company depends on third-party foundries and subcontractors and cite a limited number and geographic concentration of suppliers. The Business section adds that supplier diversification is under way, so the claim is supported with some qualification.

brief.summary: Four of five claims are Supported. Data Center revenue grew year over year in consecutive quarters (up 117% in Q2 fiscal 2027), though the company warns faster product cadence may make revenue volatile. Revenue and receivables are concentrated in a few customers. Export controls are restricting revenue: a $4.5 billion H20 charge, with licensed China sales still small. Supplier dependence is confirmed; only two foundries are named. Gross margin is Mixed evidence: 75.0% in Q2 against 72.4% a year earlier, but flat sequentially and down to 71.1% for fiscal 2026, so expansion is not established. For the overweight decision, growth supports it while concentration and export-control risk weigh against it.
unknowns: Whether year-over-year growth will continue in the quarter the next earnings report covers, since the passages describe only past results.
Whether the recast of market-platform presentation (including a reclassification between ACIE and Hyperscale) affects the comparability of prior-period Data Center figures.
How much of the growth comes from price or mix versus volume; the passages do not say.
Whether the overweight position is justified, which depends on valuation and expectations that the filings do not address.
The combined share of revenue from the largest customers is not stated, so it is not computed here.
The identities of the direct customers are not disclosed, so the passages do not show whether they are related to each other.
The indirect customer shares are described as estimates, and the passages give no figures for them.
The passages do not show whether the shift in individual customer shares in the latest quarter reflects a lasting change in concentration.
How much revenue the controls cost, since the passages give no estimate of what China sales would have been without them.
Whether the change in China revenue for the quarter ended 2026-07-26 comes from licensed H20 or H200 sales or from other products.
Whether any H200 imports will be allowed into China, and when revenue from them could begin.
How much of the growth outside China comes from demand shifted away from China.
next_steps: Check whether gross margin moves beyond the 75% plateau in the next quarter's guidance and results.
Track the share of revenue from the largest direct customers and any change in receivables concentration.
Monitor H200 license progress and any revenue from China, and the effect of export controls on other markets.
Review how the faster product cadence could affect revenue volatility and supplier capacity.
brief.status_note: Part of the thesis could not be assessed with verified evidence. The reasons are listed under coverage limits.
